title: Cutting a handle open
claim: Cutting a handle open. The Fano plane has 16 torus embeddings (7 hexagons each) and census 58 has 36. On each, the knot's signs satisfy the face condition, and twisting the signs along a non-contractible cut curve keeps every face condition but leaves a system on which the knot no longer fails. Uniting the near side's solutions over the four homology sectors forgets both homology parities: the handle cut open. (1) This removes all creation on some embeddings and not on others (Fano plane into census 6 and 38: 16 of 16; into census 14, 21 and 58: 8 of 16; into census 45: 12 of 16; census 58 into K4^(3): 36 of 36, into census 6: 28 of 36, into the Fano plane: 24 of 36), while most crossing knots survive. (2) The outcome depends on where the cut curves run, not only on their homology classes: on the Fano > Fano splice, 20 cuts per embedding in the same classes split 25 to 55 between removing all creation and not, on each of four embeddings. (3) Dropping one parity, which leaves a cylinder, cuts the 240 new knots at the Fano splices' creating removals to 17, 23 or 9. Uniting with one near point flipped (the control) never removes creation (104 of 104). So the homology parities carry most of a handle's creation, but forgetting them is not canonical in point values, and the reading that a handle creates exactly what its homology parities add fails as stated.
failure_conditions: A torus embedding of the Fano plane or census 58 on which the knot's signs violate the face condition.
A point-flip control union that removes creation at a creating removal.
Cutting the handle open removing creation for every embedding and splice (the reading would then be embedding-free).
foundation_claim_scope: Splices whose near side is the Fano plane or census 58, with the near solutions united over the homology sectors of each torus embedding.
